newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa launches U.K.-style homeless magazine.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa launches U.K.-style homeless magazine.

text.p: A South African version of the popular British magazine for the homeless, The Big Issue, was launched in Cape Town on Thursday.
In Britain homeless people sell the magazine, which is also largely produced by the homeless, and get a share of the selling price, giving them an income to ease their plight.
South Africa already has an equivalent, Homeless Talk, sold on the streets of the biggest city, Johannesburg, for two rands (43 cents), most of which goes to the vendors who are homeless themselves.
Charmaine Bruins, the editor of The Big Issue South Africa, said they would also contract the homeless to sell the magazine so that they could make a living.
"We aim to empower and create employment for homeless people so that they can be independent," she told Reuters.
"Our first issue has a print order of 14,000 and hopefully we hope to grow from strength to strength," she said. The magazine will first be published in Cape Town.
South Africa faces a huge housing backlog and thousands of homeless people live on the streets of major cities.
An all-race census conducted two months ago will clarify how many homeless there are.
